ChangeFocusBaseState.description:
WHY a target's `base_ref` is empty or set — resolves the `base_ref==""`
overload into an explicit, observable state (Gap #3).

- `incremental`: `base_ref` is a real prior-run SHA; a diff is rendered.
- `first_run`: no prior successful run for this repo yet.
- `unchanged`: prior head SHA == current HEAD SHA (full scan, no wasted diff).
- `provider_unsupported`: the provider couldn't resolve a base (e.g. branch
  pagination cap in `ref_validation.branch_ref_exists`) — reserved for a
  future producer; `_derive_diff_focus` does not emit this value today
  (an unresolved HEAD omits the repo entirely rather than recording a row).
ChangeFocusBaseState.title: ChangeFocusBaseState

ChangeFocusTarget.description:
One backend-derived change-focus target for one attached repo.

provider/repository_identity name WHICH attached repo (an App may attach
several). `head_ref` is the commit SHA this run scanned (the durable
per-repo cursor the next run reads); `base_ref` is the prior successful
run's `head_ref`, or "" on a first/unchanged run. `base_state` co-carries
WHY `base_ref` is empty (or not) — `first_run`, `unchanged`, or
`provider_unsupported` all render as `base_ref==""`, but only `base_state`
distinguishes them (Gap #3); it defaults to `"incremental"` so rows stored
before this field existed still validate. The run clones a real git
worktree per repo, so the agent diffs these refs (`git diff
base...head`) — the backend only resolves them. NOT a scope fence: it
steers, it never narrows targets.

`worktree_name` is the directory name the run's git worktree clones to
(same value `app.shared.utils.repo_path_utils.worktree_dir_name`
produces for `_repository_roots`) — `_change_focus_line` renders
`./<worktree_name>/`, not `repository_identity` (a GitLab identity is a
numeric project ID, useless prose for the agent). Defaults to `""` so
rows persisted before this field existed still validate; `_change_focus_
line` falls back to `repository_identity` when empty (legacy rows still
render something, just not a worktree path).
ChangeFocusTarget.title: ChangeFocusTarget

FindingPublic.description:
Response shape for a single Finding — only client-rendered fields.

NEVER includes: signature (internal dedup key), raw finding_metadata (the
FE reads the derived owasp/cwe/cve fields instead), or any raw internal
column not rendered by the FE.

Two orthogonal axes, both rendered by the FE's triage rail:
- status — agent-owned, the 4-state model
  (open/needs_verification/resolved/dismissed).
- triage_state — human-owned work tracking on an OPEN or NEEDS_VERIFICATION
  finding.

`manually_resolved` splits the one status the two axes share. A RESOLVED
finding is either a scan's PoC-replay proof or a human's own verdict, and
only the second one a human may undo — so the FE cannot decide whether to
offer Reopen without it. It is a derived bool, not the raw
`manually_resolved_by` UUID, because the FE renders the choice, not the
actor.
FindingPublic.title: FindingPublic

FindingStatus.description:
Agent-owned finding lifecycle status — a 4-state model.

Mirrored 1:1 from the finding's folder in app-memory/ at sync()
(open/ → open, resolved/ → resolved, dismissed/ → dismissed,
needs-verification/ → needs_verification). A finding in open/ is a
reproduced, proven vulnerability — there is no verified/regressed/stale
nuance. NEEDS_VERIFICATION is a lead the agent could not confirm
(it needs a second tenant's session, an admin console with no signup, or an
unreachable state), so instead of silently dropping it he parks it here for
a human to reconfirm. It is NOT proven (never counted as an open finding)
and NOT closed (never counted as resolved/dismissed).
FindingStatus.title: FindingStatus

RunLaunchRequest.description:
Request body for POST /appsec/apps/{app_id}/runs.

run_scope narrows the App's scope for this run — MUST be ⊆ app.scope.
Omit or pass null for a full-scope run. mode and intensity are
optional — when omitted (None), the use case applies the backend default
(Mode.BLACK / app.default_intensity). The default lives in
launch_run only, not here. scan_mode is optional too — omitted (None)
coalesces to incremental in the use case (the single default source); pass
"full" for a deep whole-worktree sweep (moot for gray/black).

Note an App with NO prior SUCCESS run always runs "full": the use case
coerces scan_mode on a first run, so an explicit "incremental" here is
honoured only once a successful run exists to diff against.
RunLaunchRequest.title: RunLaunchRequest

RunResult.description:
Pentest run lifecycle result: running | success | failed | cancelled.

Lifecycle only — NOT a verdict. A finished run is SUCCESS whether or not it
found vulnerabilities; the "found something" signal lives in the run's
finding counts (FE colors the count), never a distinct result value. FAILED
means the run could not complete honestly (sync failure, missing owner,
unexpected error) — its findings may be unwritten, so it must not read SUCCESS.
RunResult.title: RunResult

ScanMode.description:
Per-run change-focus policy: incremental|full.

incremental — focus on the git diff between the prior SUCCESSFUL run's HEAD
              and this run's HEAD (the historic always-on white-box
              behaviour). `_derive_diff_focus` keeps each repo's `base_ref`
              so the agent diffs `base...head`.
full        — a deep sweep: `_derive_diff_focus` FORCES `base_ref=""` on
              every target so no diff is rendered and the whole worktree is
              scanned. The cursor `head_ref` is still recorded so the NEXT
              incremental run has a base to diff from.

DEFAULT for both manual and scheduled runs is INCREMENTAL (the use case, not
the column, is the source of that default). MOOT for gray/black-box runs:
they clone no worktree, so there is nothing to diff and scan_mode is inert.

INVARIANT (first run): on an App with NO prior SUCCESS run,
`launch_run_with_outcome` COERCES this column to FULL regardless of what the
caller asked for — interactive or scheduled. INCREMENTAL means "diff since
the last successful run"; with no prior success there is no base, so the
value would lie to both the user and the agent. A schedule's frozen
INCREMENTAL is therefore honoured only from its first post-success fire
onward; the schedule row itself is never rewritten.
ScanMode.title: ScanMode

SurfaceSource.description:
Where a surface item came from — its PROVENANCE, not its liveness.

Liveness ("is it still there?") is unknowable to a black-box probe, so we
do NOT encode it as a status. We encode the one thing that IS provable and
that carries real risk — where the endpoint was found (matches how ASM /
API-discovery tools model shadow vs documented surface):

- DOCUMENTED — declared in the app's spec/context (OpenAPI, runbook, links).
               The expected, known surface.
- SHADOW     — discovered by the agent probing/crawling but ABSENT from the
               docs. Undocumented attack surface — the high-value signal.

A row is never deleted, never hidden, never downgraded. Freshness is the
`last_seen_run` stamp plus the agent's free-text notes in `properties`; it
is deliberately NOT a stored state (absence from a run proves nothing).

Target type. The one open plugin axis (§A/§B).

TicketComplianceStatus.description:
How well the MR satisfies its linked ticket's acceptance criteria.

Only meaningful when the review found a linked Jira/Linear ticket and read
its acceptance criteria (the reviewer already fetches these via the
reviewing-jira / reviewing-linear skill). Absent (NULL) when no ticket was
linked — the detail's compliance card then hides rather than claiming
coverage it never assessed.

Stored as its string value in a VARCHAR column, never a native Postgres
enum, so UPPER()/LOWER() and enum-type migrations (DB-02) never enter the
picture — same treatment as the sibling SnapshotFileChangeType. Lives here
(data/models) rather than in api/schemas so the column can be typed with it
and the write path stops passing bare strings; api/schemas re-exports it for
the response model. The agent-facing tool declares the same value set as an
inline Literal (the repo prefers inline Literals in model-visible schemas
over $ref/$defs); a parity test pins the two equal.
TicketComplianceStatus.title: TicketComplianceStatus

TriageState.description:
Human work-tracking on an open finding — NOT a finding status.

Answers "is a person working this?", which `FindingStatus` cannot: a finding
is equally OPEN whether nobody has looked at it or an engineer has been
fixing it all week. The two axes compose into the UI's triage rail
(open+NONE = "needs triage", open+IN_PROGRESS, open+AWAITING_RETEST,
resolved = "verified fixed"). A human reconfirming a NEEDS_VERIFICATION
lead reuses AWAITING_RETEST — it flags the finding for the next scan, no new
TriageState value is minted for it.

Ownership is strictly split: the agent owns `status` (mirrored from the
app-memory folder at sync()), a human owns this. A human value can never sit
in `status` — sync() rewrites that column from the tree every run and would
destroy it. AWAITING_RETEST is a LABEL, not a trigger: it flags the finding
for the next scan, it does not launch one.

Cleared to NONE by sync() when the agent resolves the finding — the question
this was tracking is settled.
TriageState.title: TriageState

WorkspaceRole.description:
Workspace-level roles for RBAC.

Role hierarchy (highest to lowest):
- ADMIN: Full control within workspace
- DEVELOPER: Can use chat, view resources, manage recommendations
- VIEWER: Read-only access
- SYSTEM: The workspace's own non-login actor for background work; never assignable

Note: OWNER is deprecated. Use organization-level roles instead:
- ORG_OWNER/ORG_ADMIN inherit to ADMIN in all workspaces
- ORG_DEVELOPER inherits to DEVELOPER in all workspaces
- ORG_VIEWER inherits to VIEWER in all workspaces

post.description:
Export every finding matching the caller's list filters as one PDF.

Deliberately takes no `page`/`take`: the export covers the whole filtered
set, not the page the client happens to have loaded. Board view omits
`status` (each board column IS a status set), which reads here as "all".

`status` is repeatable, matching the list endpoint exactly. The table sends
the one status it is filtered by; keeping the two endpoints on the same
shape is what lets the workspace hand its list filters straight to the
export without translating them.

post.description: Create a short-lived device authorization for an outbound-only CLI.
Poll until approved, denied, expired, or asked to slow down.

Exchange a one-time code + PKCE verifier for a Token.

Any failure (missing / expired code, verifier mismatch) returns the same
generic 400 so a stolen code cannot be probed for its state (CA-SP-3).

Logout user by revoking refresh token.

This is a best-effort operation that always succeeds. The refresh token is
read from the httpOnly cookie first, falling back to the body for legacy
clients. Auth cookies are always cleared. If the refresh token is invalid
or already revoked, we still return success.

Refresh access token with mandatory rotation.
Following Auth0 best practices.

The refresh token is read from the httpOnly cookie first, falling back to
the request body for legacy header-based clients during the migration. The
organization_id is derived from the workspace_id. If no workspace is
provided, falls back to the user's oldest active organization membership.
